manifesto.title: Building for results,
paras: This volume collects the work of the last two years: storefronts rebuilt for the Gulf, campaigns tuned to return on ad spend, and interfaces drawn with the discipline of print. The clients arrive with briefs. The briefs ask for traffic, for sales, for something measurable. What follows is the answer to those briefs — set in spreads, with every number verified against a live dashboard rather than a slide deck.

There is no house style. There are house habits: a preference for the grid over the decoration, for the metric over the vanity, for the slow reveal over the loud announcement. I stay on the accounts after launch, which means the figures on these pages are lived rather than estimated. When a conversion rate doubles, it doubles on a dashboard I can point to.
What follows is offered plainly. The work is for brands that want results, and it was never meant for everyone.

work.title: Spreads
work.intro: Five projects, set as spreads: the brief, the build, the numbers.

projects.title: Paris Chic UAE
projects.subtitle: Luxury eyewear storefront
projects.headline: A regional fashion storefront rebuilt for the Gulf.
projects.sub: Every hardcoded string moved into a translation layer — 138 keys across 19 sections, English and Arabic in sync.
projects.note: The brief was localization done properly: fluid mobile navigation, fast product discovery, and a store that reads as native in Arabic rather than translated. We audited all seven custom sections, moved every string into a translation layer, unified the button system site-wide, and locked product media to a 4:5 ratio so the grid never shifts.
projects.pullquote: A store that reads as native in Arabic, rather than translated into it.
details: Full Arabic localization with a 138-key translation layer, RTL-aware sections
Unified button system site-wide: primary, secondary, tertiary, hover states
Trust signals placed directly under Add to Cart — shipping, returns, secure checkout
Compact header reduced 24%, product media locked to 4:5 with no layout shift
Per-slide hero text colour scheme, mobile-first story section, accordion menu

projects.title: Paris Chic KSA
projects.subtitle: Saudi market fork + Virtual Try-On
projects.headline: One theme, two markets — and an AI try-on built end to end.
projects.sub: Currency AED to SAR, market switch to /ar, UAE-only content stripped, and a virtual try-on feature from theme section to encrypted worker secret.
projects.note: The UAE theme forked for Saudi Arabia against a 21-section copy spec. We stripped Dubai-specific content, switched currency and locale, rewrote the product and cart pages with Saudi trust signals, and shipped a Virtual Try-On: an RTL-aware Liquid section that composites the frame in-browser, then re-renders it photorealistically through a Cloudflare Worker.
projects.pullquote: The customer photo only leaves the browser when they press the button. The API key never leaves the worker.
details: Virtual Try-On: RTL-aware Liquid section, in-browser frame composite, photorealistic re-render via Cloudflare Worker
Customer photo only sent on explicit action; API key held as an encrypted Worker secret
Market switch AED → SAR, language switcher /ar-ae → /ar, Saudi product page trust trio
Saudi copy pass across hero, FAQ, cart and product page — 1,039 lines added
Compliance tracked against the client copy spec with a gap analysis document

projects.title: GTV Egypt
projects.subtitle: B2B fittings storefront + AI sales agent
projects.headline: A Polish hardware brand, sold like an Egyptian one.
projects.sub: 38 products rewritten in GTV's own marketing language, Arabic-first with an English edition, WhatsApp checkout, and a catalogue-trained agent that hands off to a human.
projects.note: GTV sells certified furniture fittings into Egypt, where B2B deals close on WhatsApp rather than on cards. We rebuilt all 38 products in GTV's own playbook — certified number first, mechanism second, benefit last — drew a black-and-gold identity for GTV EGYPT, wired cart and checkout into WhatsApp with prefilled order context, and trained a Gemini agent on the full catalogue so it qualifies a carpenter one question at a time before handing the conversation to Mahmoud.
projects.pullquote: In Egyptian B2B, checkout is a WhatsApp message — so every path on the site ends there.
details: 38-product catalogue with SKUs, specs and EGP pricing across five categories
Arabic-first RTL build with a complete English edition behind one toggle
Cart and checkout funneled to WhatsApp with prefilled order context; COD and tiered delivery
Custom black-and-gold GTV EGYPT identity: monogram, favicon, wordmark
Gemini sales agent trained on the full catalogue — qualifies, quotes, hands off on WhatsApp

projects.title: BurgerBite
projects.subtitle: Restaurant site with WhatsApp ordering
projects.headline: A local burger joint, online in two days.
projects.sub: Full menu with EGP prices, WhatsApp ordering, click-to-call and the Google rating — one Arabic-first page, live in days.
projects.note: Small restaurants do not need a 40-page store; they need one fast page that turns a Google search into a WhatsApp order. We put the full menu with prices, a one-tap order button, phone, map, the 4.7 Google rating and customer quotes above the fold — and went from brief to live in two days.
projects.pullquote: For a restaurant, the homepage is not a brochure — it is the till.
details: Arabic-first RTL one-pager: full menu by category with EGP pricing
Order flow funneled to WhatsApp; tap-to-call from every screen
Trust above the fold: 4.7 Google rating, 500+ monthly orders, testimonials
Static build on Vercel — loads fast on Egyptian mobile networks
Brief to live site in two days

projects.title: Roqqei
projects.subtitle: Egyptian women's fashion — built & scaled
projects.headline: A live Egyptian brand, audited, rebuilt, and scaled.
projects.sub: Store audit, product pages rebuilt, prospecting and retargeting launched, checkout optimized, conversion tracking installed. Every number verified.
projects.note: Roqqei is the proof of work that cannot be borrowed: a live Egyptian fashion brand I built and scaled. The store opened at a 0.49% conversion rate with no structured campaigns. We rebuilt the product pages, restructured the Meta account into prospecting and retargeting, and instrumented conversion tracking end to end.
projects.pullquote: From 0.49% to over 1% — every figure verified on a live dashboard, not estimated.
details: Conversion rate lifted from 0.49% to over 1%
4.2x average ROAS, CPA as low as EGP 42 per purchase
EGP 1M+ revenue and 814 orders generated
Structured Meta Ads account: prospecting, retargeting, conversion tracking

items.title: Shopify & E-commerce Systems
items.body: Designing and building high-converting storefronts for the MENA region. Custom Liquid theme development, metafield and metaobject architecture, AJAX cart flows, and mobile checkout optimization.

items.title: Performance Marketing
items.body: Meta and Google campaigns built for ROAS, not vanity metrics. Prospecting and retargeting for e-commerce, search and display for B2B, with conversion tracking wired end to end.

items.title: Front-end Engineering
items.body: Interactive web experiences with React, Next.js, and TypeScript. Kinetic typography, fluid animation, API integration, and clean component architecture.

items.title: International Shopify
items.body: Multi-market builds for brands expanding across the Gulf and beyond: localized storefronts, currency and locale switching, bilingual EN/AR content, and AI features such as virtual try-on.

about.title: About
about.bio: I treat web development like print design: rigid grids, intentional typography, and uncompromising speed. Based in Egypt, I build custom digital experiences and Shopify stores for brands across the region — and I stay on the metrics after launch, so the numbers on this page are lived, not estimated.
